messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER  Elevated KMS errors detected for GCP KMS (asia-southeast1). Symptoms: asymmetric-sign RPCs timing out, node init failing with signing handshake errors, and increased 5xx from KMS. Paging oncall.
lee (oncall): taking it. Starting a short timeline and will collect traces.
anika (sre): I'm online. Graphs show a sharp spike in KMS 99p latency at 23:12 UTC; our bootstrap path uses a 2500ms sign timeout. Lots of nodes in that region failing to reach RUNNING. Any customer noise?
fiona (cs): multiple customers in APAC reporting failed deployments and onboarding errors. Marked 6 customers as affected; escalating to high touch.
diego (runtime): pasting node excerpt:```
2026-05-14T23:12:37Z ERROR signer: AsymmetricSignTimeout key=projects/redwood/locations/asia-southeast1/cryptoKeys/serv-1 timeout_ms=2500
2026-05-14T23:12:39Z ERROR bootstrap: sign failed, aborting init, attempt=4
2026-05-14T23:12:53Z WARN process: boot loop detected, killing pod
```
lee (oncall): preliminary impact: node bootstrap failures causing some autoscale pools to underprovision; a subset of traffic routed to older nodes, causing tail latency increases and occasional 502s. Not global yet but regionally significant.
anika (sre): initial hypothesis: GCP KMS control plane in asia-southeast1 is exhibiting transient backend throttling. Our synchronous signing during bootstrap amplifies failure surface. Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) enable local ephemeral signing-cache for critical keys so bootstrap can complete; 2) switch bootstrap to an async-sign path that lets the node come up and complete signing in background; 3) temporarily increase bootstrap sign timeout to 10s.
diego (runtime): we have a lightweight local signer (runtime/local-signer:canary) that caches CSR and returns temporary attestations. Also can flip BOOTSTRAP_SIGN_TIMEOUT_MS. I'll prepare canary.
ops-bot: queued config patch for canary nodes: set BOOTSTRAP_SIGN_TIMEOUT_MS=10000 and enable local_sign_cache=true.
lee (oncall): opening GCP support case and attaching logs.
gcp-support: Case GS-20260514-314 attached. GCP acknowledges elevated latency and is investigating internal throttling in KMS control plane.
diego (runtime): canary results: enabling local cache + timeout bump allowed 9/10 canary nodes to become Ready (previously 4/10). Boot time is slightly longer but nodes reach Ready and reconcile later. Pasting reconcile log snippet:```
2026-05-14T23:17:02Z INFO signer/local: returned ephemeral token from cache, reconcile_job=queued id=job-7
2026-05-14T23:17:40Z INFO signer/reconcile: sign succeeded, token replaced id=job-7
```
anika (sre): good. Roll to region with 15s stagger. Also enable a temporary circuit-breaker so that if KMS error rate >10% we automatically prefer local cache or failover provider.
lee (oncall): contact customers team and draft proactive message. fiona, can you notify impacted customers?
fiona (cs): sending initial outreach now. also scheduling a dedicated bridge for top customers.
ops-bot: GCP case update at 23:22 UTC: 'Identified service-side throttling affecting KMS AsymmetricSign path in region; engineers deploying mitigations.' No ETA provided.
anika (sre): telemetry during roll: bootstrap failure rate in asia-southeast1 dropped from 24% -> 3.5% within 10m after canary. Instance churn reduced and onboarding API 5xx count decreased.
diego (runtime): additional safety: toggled KMS_PROVIDER_FALLBACK=aws-kms-eu for control-plane signs if local cache miss and GCP sign has retried 3x. We validated cryptographic compatibility for short-lived control tokens.
lee (oncall): note compliance check we consulted security: short-term cross-provider signing for control-plane tokens is allowed under emergency policy; logged in emergency-crypto-usage.
anika (sre): created incident ticket RID-20260514-215555 and set severity P1 due to customer-visible provisioning failures. Pager duty notified.
fiona (cs): customers receiving proactive messages between 23:20-23:30 UTC; a few asked for timelines, one requested escalation to their account team.
diego (runtime): runtime followups: add idempotency markers to reconcile jobs to avoid double token issuance; ensure reconcile is bounded and won't leak memory under heavy backlog. Created tasks RUNTIME-2028 and RUNTIME-2029.
anika (sre): handoff plan: Lee will own communications and customer bridge for next 90m; I'll take overnight monitoring after. Leave runbook notes here.
lee (oncall): I'm staying for handoff. Also enabling a synthetic bootstrap probe that runs sign calls against GCP KMS every 30s and alerts if p95 > 2s for 2 consecutive minutes.
ops-bot: Synthetic probe created: probe-kms-bootstrap-asia-southeast1. Alert threshold configured.
gcp-support: Update at 23:45 UTC: 'Control plane mitigation in place; observed reduction in AsymmetricSign latency. Continuing to monitor.'
anika (sre): monitoring window: no new bootstrap regressions in last 20m; calling for final checks.
diego (runtime): planning long-term fixes: 1) default async bootstrap for ephemeral nodes, 2) build a multi-provider signing client with automatic, crypto-safe failover, 3) add KMS health hedging in our SDK (call two providers and use first response) for critical short-lived tokens. Opening tickets RUNTIME-2030, SEC-4001.
fiona (cs): compiling customer impact timeline for postmortem: incident start 23:12 UTC; peak bootstrap failures between 23:12-23:22 UTC; mitigations rolled at 23:17-23:25 UTC; region stabilized ~23:55 UTC. Notified impacted customers and scheduling follow-ups.
lee (oncall): final note: incident set to monitoring. If graphs stay green for 1h we'll close. Leaving detailed runbook edits and action items in the incident ticket. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
